summary: Brief 5xx flood: proxy connection thrashing triggered by tenant reshard + runtime hot-swap
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled tenant reshard for a large dedicated customer (ByteDocs Inc.) we observed a short (~12 minute) but severe elevation in 5xx responses from the public API. The API Gateway returned a mix of 502 and 503 errors; upstream metrics show rapid connection churn and a burst of runtime restarts correlated with a hot-swap of runtime shards.

Impact:
- ByteDocs experienced elevated error rates (~40-60% failed requests) for 12 minutes across several production routes (generation and embeddings).
- Latency spiked for successful requests.
- No data loss reported; errors were 5xx transients.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1), Dedicated pool serving ByteDocs Inc.
- Running model variants rw_instruct_v1 (quantized) and gptj-6b for fallback.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Orchestration triggered tenant reshard to rebalance load (internal scheduled operation).
2) Prefetch invalidations were issued to new shard set; many in-flight connections hit half-close/FIN_WAIT scenarios.
3) Edge-proxy connection accounting undercounted reused TLS sessions during simultaneous runtime hot-swap.
4) Proxy started aggressively tearing down sockets and re-establishing connections, causing upstream connection saturation and short-lived runtime OOMs/restarts.
5) API Gateway returned 502/503 until keepalive and throttler settings were adjusted.

Observed logs / traces (highlights):
- api-gateway: "upstream response timeout" and repeated "502 no healthy upstream" at 2026-03-14T14:03Z
- edge-proxy: connection reset bursts and many sockets in TIME_WAIT/FIN_WAIT (see logs: /var/log/proxy/edge-2026-03-14.log, lines 1021-1240)
- runtime: short-lived process restarts with NVML driver warnings at 14:05Z; prefetch invalidation flood recorded in Serving traces
- Datadog dashboard (proxy.conn.reuse.rate) shows reuse counter dropping sharply and reconnects spiking

Temporary mitigation applied during incident:
- Rolled back the reshard operation to previous shard set (orchestration) to stop new invalidations.
- Increased proxy keepalive and connection reuse window temporarily at the edge (toggle: edge.proxy.keepalive=90s).
- Raised throttler concurrency cap for the tenant to avoid mass rejections during reconnections.

Next steps / follow-up (see investigation_notes and resolution_notes):
- Postmortem planned; lower-level fix required in proxy TLS session accounting and a safer prefetch invalidation ordering during reshard.

2026-03-14T14:21:00Z - Daniel Kim (SRE): Observed edge-proxy conn churn and high TIME_WAIT. Correlates with tenant reshard job. Assigning to runtime on-call for quick rollback option.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: TLS session reuse counter bug in edge-proxy + simultaneous prefetch invalidations caused a reconnect storm that exposed a throttling hole in the API Gateway leading to 502/503 responses.

Datapoints:
- spike in edge.conn.reconnects: +1200 reconnections/min at peak (14:02-14:06Z)
- runtime restarts: 7 restarts across 3 nodes correlated to reconnects and short-lived memory pressure
- CPU on edge-proxy nodes spiked ~35% but not saturated; socket table exhaustion observed in kernel metrics (netstat counters).
Traces: Full distributed traces attached (trace ids list in confluence page). Prefetch invalidation events arrived in scrambled order after reshard, increasing race window.

Reproduction attempts in staging: We simulated rapid reshard + invalidation using a dedicated test tenant and reproduced elevated reconnects but did not trigger runtime restarts until we introduced a prefetch cancellation storm.
resolution_notes: Immediate: Rolled back the reshard, temporarily disabled prefetch invalidations during shard operations, and increased proxy keepalive window. These actions reduced reconnect churn and eliminated the 5xx flood.

Medium-term: Engineering to patch proxy TLS session accounting to correctly handle simultaneous reuse and release cycles. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2831 (proxy accounting + safer reconnect handling).

Long-term: Update orchestration to perform reshard in smaller increments and serialize prefetch invalidations with acknowledgment handshake. Add canary validation and healthchecks that block prefetch invalidations if reconnection rate exceeds threshold.
Customer follow-up: CS scheduled a postmortem review with ByteDocs for 2026-03-18. Commitment: provide timeline for patch and an ETA for deployment to staging within 5 business days.
Tags for runbook update: proxy-keepalive-tuning, reshard-safety, prefetch-invalidations
